1:?Scope: Mechanical removal of existing suction outlet cover and sump.

A:?Process: Hand-chipping of the gunite shell surrounding the main drain to a depth sufficient to expose at least 3 inches of the existing PVC suction line.

B:? Connection: Installation of a new VGB-compliant (ANSI/APSP-16) deep-sump pot. The connection to the existing 2-inch (or 3-inch) Schedule 40 PVC plumbing will be made using high-pressure PVC primer and solvent cement (IPS Weld-On 711 or equivalent).

C: ?Compliance Note: The new sump will be configured to meet the manufacturer's specific "field-fabricated" or "factory-manufactured" sump requirements to prevent suction entrapment.

?2. Hydrostatic Pressure Testing

A: ?Protocol: Prior to the gunite patch, the suction line will be isolated.

B: ?Test: The line will be pressurized to 25 PSI (or 5 PSI above operating pressure) using a calibrated pressure gauge.

?C: Verification: The pressure will be held for a minimum of 30 minutes with zero drop in PSI to verify the integrity of the new solvent weld connection and the existing underground piping within the zone of repair.

?3. Structural Gunite Patch & Bonding
?Preparation: The interior surface of the chipped gunite "bowl" will be wire-brushed and cleaned of all loose debris.

?A: Bonding: A cementitious bonding agent (slurry coat) will be applied to the old gunite to ensure a monolithic bond between the existing shell and the new patch.

B: ?Patching: The void will be filled with high-strength 4,000 PSI hydraulic concrete or pool-grade gunite mix, hand-packed to eliminate air pockets (voids) around the sump and piping.

C: ?Finish: The patch will be finished approximately 1/2" below the existing shell surface to allow for the application of the final waterproof interior finish ( white plaster) to be flush with the new VGB drain frame
